as_told.title: Condon Committee wrote its conclusion before the study was finished

tellings.quote: After considering various possibilities, the AFOSR staff decided to ask the University of Colorado to undertake the project (see Preface).

The decision to discontinue UFO investigations was based on an evaluation of a report prepared by the University of Colorado entitled, "Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects;" a review of the University of Colorado's report by the National Academy of Sciences; past UFO studies and Air Force experience investigating UFO reports during the 40s, '50s, and '60s.

plain: The Air Force's long-running UFO study, Project Blue Book, ended after a university review that, Karl Nell says, had its answer written before the work was done. Blue Book was the US Air Force's UFO investigation of the 1950s and 60s. Nell is a guest speaking from an official background. He tells Michels that the Air Force commissioned a study from the University of Colorado, led by Edward Condon, who had worked on the Manhattan Project, and that Condon "wrote the conclusion of the study before the study was complete" and bragged about it. The same claim comes up again in a second episode, without the bragging. If true, it would mean the official end of UFO research was decided in advance. The study itself, "Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects", published by the University of Colorado on October 31, 1968, says the Air Force Office of Scientific Research "decided to ask the University of Colorado to undertake the project". The report says nothing about when its conclusions were written, so the claim that they were written early does not come from the report. A 1985 Air Force fact sheet gives the record's side of the ending: "The decision to discontinue UFO investigations was based on an evaluation" of the Colorado report, a review of it by the National Academy of Sciences, and the Air Force's own experience in the 40s, 50s and 60s.

discussion.by: Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects (the Condon report, 1968)
discussion.text: The report says the Air Force Office of Scientific Research asked the University of Colorado to undertake the study; it does not speak to when its conclusions were written, so the claim that Condon wrote them before the study was complete does not rest on the report.
